title: Monetary Policy Report—January 2026
summary: The Bank of Canada held its target overnight rate at 2.25% (Bank Rate 2.5%, deposit rate 2.20%), maintaining a neutral stance as US tariffs continue to disrupt the Canadian economy while CPI inflation remains near the 2% target. The Governing Council projects Canadian economic growth to average around 1¼% over the projection horizon, with excess supply roughly offsetting upward cost pressures.
key_points: Bank of Canada maintains target overnight rate at 2.25% with Bank Rate at 2.5% and deposit rate at 2.20%
CPI inflation remains close to the 2% target, consistent with the Bank's inflation control strategy
US tariffs and trade uncertainty are weighing on economic growth, which was subdued in 2025
Canadian businesses are actively adapting by expanding exports to non-US markets and reducing reliance on US imports
The Canada–United States–Mexico Agreement (CUSMA/USMCA) is under review, adding significant uncertainty to the trade outlook
Global growth is expected to remain solid, supported by AI investment boom and fiscal stimulus in major economies
Governing Council includes Governor Tiff Macklem, Senior Deputy Governor Carolyn Rogers, and Deputies Toni Gravelle, Sharon Kozicki, Nicolas Vincent, Rhys Mendes, and Michelle Alexopoulos
why_it_matters: This quarterly monetary policy report provides the official outlook of the Bank of Canada on the Canadian economy, including inflation trajectory and growth prospects. The decision to hold rates steady signals a cautious, data-dependent approach amid unprecedented trade uncertainty from US tariff policy. Market participants tracking Canadian dollar, Canadian bonds, and trade-sensitive equities will find this essential for positioning.
macro_context: The Bank of Canada's projections assume US tariffs remain elevated with high uncertainty about future trade arrangements. The Canadian economy is undergoing structural adjustments as businesses seek alternative export markets and reduce dependency on US supply chains. Excess supply conditions are expected to balance upward cost pressures from tariffs, keeping inflation near the 2% target over the projection horizon. Geopolitical uncertainty is flagged as unusually high.
